No, I moved to Porto in 2023.

Since 2023. I really like it, and I’ve made some good friends.

Yes, I started a photography group in 2025.
Do you still go every week?
I do. We meet on Sundays. What’s changed in your life?

A is more expensive, but it has two beds.
B is cheaper. Is one bed enough for two friends?
Not for me. I’d like my own bed, and A is closer to the centre.
That’s true. B is a twenty-minute walk away.

The price, but I can pay more if we both have a bed.

Welcome back! Yeah, I’ve been painting all week.
It’s great! Have you finished?
Almost. I’ve painted both rooms, the living room and the kitchen. The bedroom is next.
And your shoes! Have you been running?
Yes! I’ve been running every morning for two weeks.
Every morning? Wow. And there’s a cake on the table. You’ve even been baking!
Ha! Yes. I’ve baked three cakes this week. Anyway, how was Korea?
Great! I visited my family and ate a lot. But I have jet lag. I’ve been sleeping all day!
Oh no! You seem tired. Here, have some cake.
Of course! I always say yes to cake.

The show was great, but it had already started when we arrived.
What time did you get there?
At eight twenty. We’d left late, and I’d forgotten my wristband at home.
Oh no. Couldn’t you just show your ticket?
The person at the entrance sent us to the help desk. We missed the opening act.
At least you got in eventually. What would you check next time?
I’d check the ticket and wristband before leaving, and allow more time.
Someone has left a backpack by our table. Should we take it to reception?
Yes. There’s a boarding pass visible in the open pocket. The owner might be travelling.
Maybe, but it could be an old pass. We don’t know the date.
True. There’s also a charger and a black notebook.
Those are common things. What detail could help reception identify it?
The notebook has a silver star, and the key ring is a red fish.
That’s more useful. Let’s let the caller describe those before we suggest them.
Agreed. We can make a guess, but we shouldn’t hand it over without checking.

I’d have more flexibility, but a longer commute.
Would the longer journey be a problem every day?
Only on three days. I could work from home twice a week.

I’m not sure yet. I’d like time for a course in the afternoon.
Then I’d ask whether the flexible hours really include afternoons.
Good idea. If they didn’t, the offer would be much less useful.

Do you work better at home or in an office?
At home, usually, because I can concentrate without interruptions.
I understand that. However, I miss the quick conversations with the team.
Me too. Although I prefer home, I wouldn’t want to work alone all week.
Would a hybrid routine solve that?
It could, if we agree on the office days. Otherwise we might all come in separately.
Good point. We could have two shared team days and keep the rest flexible.
That’s worth trying. Let’s check whether it gives us enough quiet time too.
So, how was New York?
Pretty good, but on the second day, my phone died at four in the afternoon.
Oh no! Why?
I’d been using it as a map all day, and I didn’t notice how low the battery was. And I’d left my charger at the hotel.
Why didn’t you go back to the hotel?
I tried, but I got lost. And the team dinner was at seven. The address was in a message from Raj!
So what did you do?
I asked a doorman for help, and he told me about a café. But there were no free outlets.
Oh no. And then?
I’d been waiting there alone for twenty minutes when a woman lent me her power bank. Luckily, I had my cable.
So did you make it to the dinner?
Eventually, yes. I caught a taxi and got there at eight. By then, they’d been waiting for an hour!

Can we promise the event pack will be ready by Friday morning?
The draft will be ready on Tuesday, but we need the review before making that promise.
The review is booked for Wednesday. How long will the final changes take?
About one working day after the comments arrive, provided the brief doesn’t change.
So by Thursday evening you’ll have finished the main version?
That’s the plan. On Friday morning I’ll be checking the printed copies.
What will you be doing when the volunteers arrive at ten?
I’ll be handing over the packs. Someone else needs to welcome the guests.
I can do that. What would put the handover at risk?
A late review or a new section. We should flag either as soon as it happens.
Agreed. Let’s confirm the review, then communicate the deadline with that condition.
And keep a short progress update, so nobody assumes a draft is the final version.
Do you ever wonder what life would be like if you’d stayed?
Sometimes. If I hadn’t moved to Toronto, I’d probably still be doing the same job
Would that have been a bad thing?
Not necessarily, but I wouldn’t know how much I enjoy working abroad
So moving was a turning point?
Definitely. If I hadn’t taken that chance, I wouldn’t feel this confident now
Was it easy from the start?
Not at all. I missed home and almost gave up
What made you stay?
I got an opportunity to work with a really supportive team
It sounds as though the difficult part led to something good
It did. I can see that now, even if I couldn’t see it at the time

a consequence

a setback

Someone must have been here. The plant has been moved.
Maybe, but let’s check the record before deciding who it was.
A spare key was used at five. There’s also a receipt from five twenty.
That suggests a visit, but the receipt might have been left by someone else earlier.
Could someone have come through the window?
It’s closed now. That doesn’t prove it was closed the whole afternoon.
Good point. We shouldn’t treat a current state as a complete history.
Who had permission to use the key?
The neighbour was going to water the plants, but I don’t know whether she came.
Then I’d ask her first. The camera record could be another check if needed.
So our strongest explanation is a permitted visit, not a confirmed identity yet.
Exactly. We can update that conclusion when we have more than a clue.
Why is the total higher than the booking confirmation?
The receipt includes twenty dollars for breakfast, plus a fifty-dollar deposit.
I thought breakfast was included in the room price.
It was. We needn’t have paid for the same breakfast again.
Is the deposit another mistake?
Not according to the conditions. It’s returned after the room check, if there’s no damage.
So we should keep the two amounts separate when we ask.
Exactly. We can show the confirmation and request the breakfast charge back.
Did we need to pay the full room price in advance?
No. We chose to, but the confirmation allowed payment at arrival.
That’s different from saying the room itself was free.
Yes. The issue is one duplicate service, not every payment on the receipt.
My phone screen cracked yesterday. Do you know a reliable repair shop?
Yes. I had mine repaired at a place near the station
Did you have to leave it there?
Just for the afternoon. They sent me a message when it was ready
That sounds convenient. I need to get my jacket altered as well

The sleeves are too long, so I want to have them shortened
You could get a quote before you leave it
Good point. I don’t want to pay more than the jacket cost
Ask about the collection date too. They can get busy
I will. I need it back before Friday
Then I’d call first and check that they can have it ready in time
How did the dinner planning go? Did everyone agree?
Not on everything. One person suggested having dinner on Saturday.
And someone promised to book the table?
Yes, the host promised to book after checking the group’s availability.
I heard that everyone agreed to pay in advance.
That’s not accurate. One guest refused to pay before seeing the cancellation conditions.
So suggesting dinner wasn’t the same as committing to the deposit.
Exactly. The person who suggested it also said the date was open to discussion.
Did anybody admit that the first summary was wrong?
The host did. They offered to send a corrected summary to the group.
That should help. We need to preserve what people actually intended.
Yes: a suggestion, a conditional promise and a refusal are three different things.
insist on

Which apartment would you recommend for this brief?
The person who works from home needs a usable work area, but location matters too.
A is near the metro. B has more space, although it’s further away.
And C, which has a balcony, is between them in terms of distance.
Is the balcony essential or just attractive?
Attractive. The fixed requirements are a work area and a total budget under a thousand.
Do all the listings include the maintenance fee?
A and B state a total. C’s listing doesn’t confirm the fee.
Then we shouldn’t compare the advertised rents as if they were the full costs.
Agreed. I’d arrange a viewing of A and ask C’s landlord about the missing fee.
Would B still be an alternative if the commute were manageable?
Yes. It offers more space, which could matter more than being right by the metro.
I can’t remember locking the front door
I remember seeing you turn the key
That’s reassuring. Did you remember to turn off the stove?
Yes. I checked it just before we left
I remembered to close the window, but I forgot to water the plants
That can wait until we get back
I always seem to forget something when I’m in a hurry
Maybe try keeping a short checklist by the door

I’m sorry, but the room next to the lift is too noisy for me to sleep.
I’m sorry for the disturbance. We can offer earplugs.
Thank you, but what I need is a quiet room. I have an early presentation.
I understand. Is the problem mainly the lift or the street outside?
It was the lift that woke me repeatedly. The street isn’t the main issue.
That helps us find a suitable alternative. Have you already asked for a change?
I did ask this afternoon, but I haven’t had a confirmed option yet.
I can check another room, though it may not be available immediately.
Could you tell me when it would be ready and whether it’s away from the lift?
Yes. I’ll confirm those details before asking you to move.
I appreciate that. A different room only helps if it solves the noise problem.
Agreed. I’ll come back with a specific offer rather than another general apology.
What change would you propose for our weekly study-group meeting?
I’d replace the sixty-minute status round with a short written update.
What problem would that solve?
People repeat information we could read. We need the live time for questions.
I can see the benefit. My concern is that some people won’t read the update.
That’s a fair point. Having said that, a longer meeting doesn’t guarantee attention either.
True. Could the update be short enough to read before a ten-minute discussion?
Yes. We could use three headings and keep the live slot for unresolved questions.
What about someone who thinks of a question afterwards?
We’d need a place to ask asynchronously, and someone responsible for replies.
Then I’d support a trial, provided we check whether questions actually get answered.
Agreed. In short, less reporting aloud, but a clearer way to get help.
a proposal
The proposal changes the status round.
a benefit
A possible benefit is more useful live time.
a drawback
A drawback is that updates may not be read.
a concern
We need to understand the concern.
an alternative
What alternative would preserve the purpose?
a compromise
The compromise keeps a short live discussion.
Would you support a complete phone ban at school?
I’d support restrictions, although I’m not sure a total ban would be fair
What kind of exceptions would you make?
Some students use their phones for accessibility or medical reasons
That makes sense. The main problem is distraction during lessons
Exactly. Whereas adults can choose when to check messages, younger students may need clearer boundaries
Even adults find that difficult sometimes
True. That’s why responsibility shouldn’t fall entirely on the students
So schools and families would need to agree on the rules
Yes. Despite the practical challenges, a shared approach could work better
I’d be more comfortable with that than with a rule that ignores individual needs
Me too. The aim should be better learning, not simply fewer devices
So, the big talk with Raj is tomorrow?
